scope: Additional read-only audit of fingerprint generation and first-instruction delivery on the current uncommitted optimization tree
conclusion: Not complete or fully reliable: three additional defects reproduced; none of these three defects is fixed by this audit

findings.setup: Reuse a single Chromium user-data directory across graceful browser restarts. Register a Service Worker with a top-level hardware/network snapshot under a 2-core persona; restart with the same profile ID, a different seed and a 4-core persona, retrieve the existing registration without explicitly calling register or update, and message the active worker.
findings.interpretation: The first response after the restart still exposes the prior 2-core persona. After the browser background update, the active worker has captured 5 cores with injectionInstalled=false at top level, although its later live read is the requested 4 cores. The delayed post-resume evaluator cannot change values already observed or retained by worker application code.
findings.qualification: The registration can update and replace its active worker during the test; the two responses need not come from the same worker instance. They are two distinct delivery failure stages, not a claim that a const binding was mutated. A positive workerInstalled probe denotes the token/runtime revision, not equality of all current persona values.
findings.recommendedDirection: Bind persisted Worker delivery to persona identity and runtime revision, and enforce current-persona delivery before application script evaluation. A post-resume timeout is not a first-instruction barrier. Any cache migration must be explicit and preserve user data.

findings.interpretation: The generated pool contains 10.1 Mbps; Chromium RoundMbps caps its native exposed result at 10 Mbps. Generation consistency still reports ok and runtime delivery succeeds, so configuration equality is insufficient to establish native plausibility.
findings.recommendedDirection: Validate generation and explicit overrides against the target engine bounds and quantization, add native-bound checks to consistency validation, and version any changes that would alter persisted persona replay.

findings.interpretation: A custom zero battery level is replaced by 0.87 through a falsy fallback. Explicit null durations, documented as the JSON-safe representation of Infinity, are converted to zero through Number(null). The invalid values reach navigator.getBattery(). This reproduces the custom override path and does not imply all default battery snapshots fail.
findings.recommendedDirection: Distinguish zero from absent input and null from finite durations throughout normalization and generation, then validate charging/discharging state semantics end to end.

validation.note: Prior passing suites describe existing coverage; the new concrete counterexamples invalidate any claim of perfection.

limitations: Native probes in this pass use Chromium on Linux. A Windows or iOS persona is not a native Windows or iOS device.
This audit does not certify all GPU, font, platform-specific engine, arbitrary module graph, or TLS/HTTP transport behavior.
The effectiveType/RTT statistical combination observations are not classified here as impossible native states.
